P1.evidence: The read-back was the best in the batch, and it was from his own prior-call notes rather than a setter's: 'I was going over just a few of the notes from our brief conversation earlier this week. You mentioned a few things, sound like the main one is dropping down from 90 kgs. You want to cut down, you mentioned that you're looking into calisthenics, you're wanting to not sweat a lot when you're walking with your new son, talking about your job, doing IT.' Specific and it plainly landed. But because this was a continuation, no frame was set at all for this call and no agreement was sought — reasonable in the moment, and still a miss on both, because an eighty-five minute call with no stated shape is how it ended up running eighty-five minutes. The open question ran: 'what are some of the main reasons why you're looking to get back into good shape?'

P2.evidence: Height, weight, target weight and occupation were all carried over from the 15 June call and correctly not re-asked, so they score not applicable here. Current training was re-checked properly: 'have you started any type of exercise plan recently? Are you exercising now?' → nothing. Diet was approached only through the cooking-and-shopping angle, which surfaced that his wife makes all the food decisions and that he dislikes cooking, but never established what he actually eats. The serious gap is health and injuries: across two calls totalling nearly two hours, the rep never once asked about health conditions, injuries, chronic pain or movement limitations. The prospect raised the topic himself — 'you can harm yourself so fast doing things badly ... making some pain on my body or things on the back' — and it was not picked up. Sleep and energy were never asked.

P3.evidence: Strong work under real language difficulty. The one-thing question ran cleanly: 'what exactly would you like to have happen with your body? Your weight, maybe your muscle, how you feel, over the next, let's say, six months?' → the six-pack. The follow-up is the best question the rep asked on any call in this batch: 'when you think of the version of you that is able to get the six-pack, how do you think that that guy is showing up and operating differently that's making you go, oh, I don't know if that's possible?' — which produced 'it will build more confidence, just knowing that I'm able to fix goals and to reach them.' From there the rep drove correctly outward into whether he sets goals elsewhere in life, which opened the failed photography business, and then into identity: 'I don't want to endure my life anymore, I want to own it.' Family surfaced but was never driven — the four-month-old son was mentioned by the rep as a prompt and the prospect's own 'to give the best you can to your family' was left unexplored. The reflect-back never came.

P4.evidence: The most complete Phase 4 in the batch. Past attempts and what happened were both covered, carrying forward the honeymoon story and adding the pre-wedding gym phase. Why it did not stick was challenged rather than accepted — when the prospect said he had no time, the rep pushed back properly: 'would you say that that is 100% true or it's more accurate maybe that you just were not prioritizing it?' → 'I'm not prioritizing right currently.' The gap was then named by the prospect himself: 'I need a plan. When I have a plan, I'm able to commit to it ... But when I set a goal by myself, and I'm trying to find out how to reach it by myself, I'm done.' And the scripted stick-to-it move genuinely ran, in substance if not in words: 'you can pull up ChatGPT and get a plan, but it sounds like there's something deeper than just overthinking and overplanning ... I'm guessing there's something deeper than maybe like a fear of doing the wrong thing.' The rep then landed the structural point the phase exists for: 'the question isn't really thinking about maybe your limiting beliefs or your subconscious. It's just like, well, why aren't you doing the actions?' The prospect's reply — 'Okay, I get it now. I guess I didn't until today' — is the clearest evidence of a phase landing anywhere in this batch.

P5.evidence: Never ran. No two-year question, no willingness to settle, no why-not, no line in the sand. This is the fourth consecutive sales call in this batch where Phase 5 was skipped entirely, and here it was the most costly, because the rep had just spent twenty minutes establishing that this prospect's core failure mode is deferring action — the exact thing the Consequence Frame exists to interrupt. 'You've told me you overthink instead of acting; what does that cost you over the next two years?' was sitting right there.

P6.evidence: The belief question ran well and early: 'if you had somebody to take all that thought process off of your plate and just show you, okay, Jonathan, do these workouts, here's how you do them, here's when you do them, and here's what to eat — does that doubt still exist?' → 'it will be easier for me because I will just have to just apply what is said.' The anything-else question was attempted twice — 'is there anything else outside of just the knowledge that you can see as being like a block in your journey?' — and produced the cooking issue, but it was never asked about money, which is the entire reason this call ended where it did. The rep then asked readiness in a way he himself recognised as wrong and had to restate: 'Maybe I misphrased that. I guess that's not the right question.' Critically, he did not have a clear yes before presenting: the last answer before the pitch was 'yeah, I guess yeah ... I'm just trying to find out what is the best, what is this thing that will suit me the best, and I don't know it yet.' That is hesitation, and the script says return to Phase 5. He presented instead.

P11.evidence: No close was reached. The prospect could not afford any tier including the $199/month option, the rep disqualified him on budget, and the call ended without a payment attempt. Payment, onboarding, agreement and welcome steps were all genuinely unreachable.

objection_plays.detail: Isolation ran properly: 'is there anything outside of just not having 6K available that's coming up for you? Or is it just the money?' The worth-it reframe ran and the rep was honest about the weak answer he got — 'You didn't sound very certain about that' — which is good practice. Several financial-picture questions ran: whether his wife works, what they had set aside, and where the savings were going. The rep also asked a sharp and legitimate question most reps skip: 'Considering the financial constraints, what was the plan when you came on to this call, knowing that we're probably going to ask you for money?' What did not run: cash on hand as a number, credit cards, available credit, investments, and the 'you're not in a SHOULD I place, you're in a HOW place' frame. He did probe credit — 'I'm not even sure if you have credit cards in France' — but as an aside rather than a step. The play then gave way to a descending ladder of tiers, and to the rep's credit he closed it honestly by disqualifying rather than pushing a prospect with a four-month-old and a house deposit onto credit.

'I have to speak with my wife first because I can't decide that like this' is a clean OB trigger and none of the play ran. Not one move: no 'money aside, do you personally feel this can get you there', no 'what obstacles might come up when you talk to her', no 'is there any reason she would not want you healthier'. The miss is more notable because the rep had already done the groundwork forty-five minutes earlier, establishing that Marie knows about the call and is supportive — 'she knows that we are on the call right now' and 'I know that she will do some effort to help'. He had the material to run OB and did not use it.

Script gap, and the same one as the David Elder call: no path for a prospect who wants the programme and genuinely cannot fund any version of it. Here the prospect's ceiling was roughly 100 to 200 euros per month against a $6,000 ask, and he declined the $199/month product too. The playbook offers nothing between 'open the wallet harder' and improvising downward. The rep handled it about as well as an unscripted rep can — he was honest that the cheap tier is not personalised rather than overselling it, and he disqualified plainly. Worth adding a genuine disqualification play to the script, including how to route these prospects to the free resources the setters already use.

notes: Genuinely the best discovery work in the batch on Phases 3 and 4 — the rep found the real blocker, named it, and got the prospect to see it, which is rare. Then two structural failures cost the call. First, affordability was not tested until minute sixty-five of an eighty-five minute call, despite a wedding, a failed business, a newborn and a house deposit all being disclosed in the first hour; a single money question at the thirty-minute mark would have saved both of them an hour across two calls. Second, health and injuries were never asked in nearly two hours of conversation across the pair of calls. Coach the affordability checkpoint before the presentation, and treat the P2 injury questions as non-optional regardless of how the call is flowing.
